planck_bounce_test.verdict: no bounce feature; the framework predicts beta_k = 0 at every scale

claims.statement: The Wheeler-DeWitt operator is self-adjoint with Psi(0) = 0; every self-adjoint extension gives unitary evolution through a = 0
With Psi(0) = 0 the spectrum is 2j + 3/2 and the universe is exactly periodic with period pi
A packet released at rest bounces at a universal <a>_min ~ 0.16 ell ~ 0.26 l_P
Every graviton mode is an exact oscillator of integer frequency n through the bounce; h_n stays finite
The bounce lasts Delta T ~ 0.49 ell / a_max of conformal time; gradients are suppressed as (0.49 ell / lambda_max)^2
The quantum mixmaster universe bounces at <a>_min = 0.256 (+-3 %) and re-expands
Planck 2018 shows no bounce feature: cutoff, step and Bogoliubov templates improve chi^2 by at most 1.2, 1.6 and 2.6

notes: Runs are the exact solution (odd coherent-state combination). 'paper_grid' repeats the computation with the finite differences of [QG] Sec. 21 on (0, 24) with 6000 points, which reproduces every printed peak <a^-2> and <a>_min of the Theorem Lambda table.

The printed peaks (262, 533, 1035, 1917) are below the exact values (270.7, 565.4, 1154.9, 2333.7): the grid sum misses an O(h) boundary term at a = 0, where |Psi|^2/a^2 is largest, and second-order dispersion slows the packet at large a_max (bounce delayed by 0.063 at a_max = 16).
Exact <a>_min tends to the universal sqrt(12/pi)/12 = 0.1629 ell (0.260 l_P); the printed decrease to 0.1518 at a_max = 16 is the same discretisation effect. Delta T * a_max tends to 0.481.
The paper's Figure 1 (right) is a_max = 6 on the (0, 40), 8000-point grid: see snapshots_paper_grid.
